name: Colin Gupta

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about a normal day at your accounting firm.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I start with the bicycle wholesaler's overseas invoices, because one exchange-rate line can throw its tax return off. I lead the team preparing accounts and returns; I enjoy catching that line before the owner sees a false bill, but chasing freight paperwork long after everyone has gone home gets old. I am 43, with a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification. I use AI every day to group the invoices for review, then check the bank and signed freight records myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI mostly levels off, I still have a good tool for sorting invoices, not a substitute for checking them. The wholesaler will keep shipping bicycles and asking us why a tax number changed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team to keep a named signer and the original freight records. I would tell the owner exactly what the software grouped and what I checked.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I earn above the usual rate for an accountant, and my partner Rina and I have about fourteen months of household expenses saved. Our mortgage and two school-age children keep us careful, but her pharmacy wage and plenty of nearby firms give us room if a job changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the wholesaler's paid accounts and using our approved daily AI sort with the same source check. I would ask my manager Ash to remove one duplicate invoice entry only after a paid test on last quarter's records proves the totals match; if he refuses, I would retain the current paid process.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about work and money in this picture. A faster invoice pile is pleasant, but it does not require us to redesign our lives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is in the source check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I match the freight date and rate to the bank amount before signing. A sorted list is useful only if I can trace it backwards.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use a new tool without Ash?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, client invoices are not my private playground. My manager Ash has to approve a paid historical test and the live change in writing.

say: I would keep a **named signer** and original freight records.
I would explain what AI **grouped** and what I checked.
think: Our **fourteen-month reserve** and high pay make a mild change manageable.
Rina's wage and many local firms provide **options** if this job changes.
do: Keep **paid wholesaler accounts** and approved daily AI grouping with source checks.
Remove **duplicate invoice entry** only after Ash approves a paid historical test and live change in writing; otherwise retain paid process.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and money.
S0.quote: A sorted list is useful only if I can trace it backwards.
fieldNote: He uses AI **every day** but sees value in the signed freight source and bank match.
The process change needs **paid historical proof** and written manager approval; his current reserve is already held, not new saving.

steps.text: Keep paid wholesaler returns and source-check approved daily AI invoice groups
Remove duplicate entry only after Ash approves paid historical test and live change in writing

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AI could draft the accounts, check the tax and answer the wholesaler's questions, so the office would need fewer paid hours. Robots will come more slowly for the warehouse, but my desk would feel it first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the partners to show staff the error rate before cutting the checking rota. I would argue that the person signing a return needs paid time to examine the sources.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own lead hours could shrink if the firm runs more clients through one signer. Fourteen months saved is comfortable, but our high wage pays the mortgage and school costs; Rina's pharmacy pay would not replace it all.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would run a two-week paid test of anonymised freight invoices against signed originals only with Ash's written approval. If it passes, I would train the team on the approved AI checker during paid hours and use it live only after written sign-off; if refused, I would keep the authorised paid checks. In the first year, if my hours are cut, I would take a posted senior tax job only with written pay, hours and start date covering our mortgage and the children's pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing my own paid hours, though I am happy to test a useful tool. A cheap calculation can become an expensive wrong tax bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who signs the test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ash and I would count wrong rates and missed credit notes, then put our names on the result. I want to know which errors the tool repeats.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept a longer commute?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the written wage after travel still covers our bills and Rina's confirmed pharmacy rota covers pickup. Plenty of local firms make a long commute unnecessary unless the actual offer is better.

say: I would require **error rates** before changing the rota.
I would protect **paid checking time** for the signer.
think: My own **lead hours** could fall with faster accounts.
Rina's wage cannot fully replace my **higher salary** and mortgage payments.
do: Test **two weeks** of anonymised freight invoices against signed originals on paid time with written approval; otherwise keep paid checks.
Train the team on the **approved checker** on paid time after a pass; use live only with written sign-off.
Take **posted tax work** after cuts only with written pay covering bills after travel, hours, start and confirmed pickup.
feel: I feel **anxious** about reduced paid hours.
S1.quote: A cheap calculation can become an expensive wrong tax bill.
fieldNote: Daily AI use does not erase his demand for **signed error evidence** and paid training before live deployment.
A new post needs a **written after-travel wage**, actual start date and pickup arrangement, not a verbal prospect.

steps.text: Test anonymised freight originals for two paid weeks with written approval; otherwise retain authorised paid checks
Train team on paid time after pass; use checker live only with written sign-off
Take posted job after cuts with written pay covering bills after travel, start and confirmed pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could perform the tax judgment and exchange-rate check on my screen. Robots around 2031 would later reach warehouse handling; they do not postpone a desk loss.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the partners to give staff clear notice and written severance terms. I would not tell the wholesaler that a human signature alone makes an AGI return reliable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my senior preparation role to go when AGI makes the whole file cheaper. Fourteen months of cash buys a search, but losing my high wage would still change the mortgage plan, and I have been waking early doing the sums.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would defer replacing our working car and move its planned monthly payment from my salary into job-loss cash. I would keep every paid file offered until the role actually ends; in the first year after 2028, if it does, I would use the reserve for bills while applying to posted procurement-audit jobs at local wholesalers. I would accept one only with written wage, hours and a start date that cover the mortgage and confirmed pickup, knowing that desk audit faces AGI too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect our main wage to disappear. We can wait for an actual offer; we cannot make one appear by calling a job title safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave before a cut?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for a signed offer with a start date and wages that cover our fixed bills. Otherwise I would keep paid accounts work while it is actually offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What about your family business?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My brother Arun's repair shop is not a spare salary for us. I could ask him what his books need, but I would not count his business as an offer.

say: I would ask for **written notice and severance**.
I would admit a **human signature** does not guarantee a reliable AGI return.
think: I expect my **senior preparation role** to end in 2028.
Our **fourteen-month reserve** buys search time, not a replacement wage.
do: Defer the **working-car replacement** and deposit its planned monthly payment while salary continues.
Keep **offered paid files** until the role ends; after loss, use reserve for bills during search.
Take a **posted procurement-audit job** only with written mortgage-covering wage, hours, start and confirmed pickup.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected loss of my main wage.
S2.quote: We can wait for an actual offer; we cannot make one appear by calling a job title safe.
fieldNote: The 2028 **desk shock** precedes capable warehouse robots; procurement audit remains thinking work, so he treats it as a bridge.
He creates **new cash** from a deferred car payment while employed and uses existing savings only after a real gap.

steps.text: Defer car replacement and deposit planned payment while salary continues
Keep paid files while offered; after loss use reserve for bills
After loss take posted audit job with written mortgage-covering wage hours start confirmed pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives me time to see which firms pay for someone to challenge an automated freight bill. AGI reaches the accounting desk in 2031; robots around 2034 are later for warehouses.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners for a paid route into supplier audit, with the wage and duties written down. I would tell colleagues that a course with no job behind it is a household purchase, not a career plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The ordinary tax return fee may fall, but my experience with mismatched freight documents could fit a paid audit role. I am willing to learn new software, provided the employer shows a real place to use it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would enrol in the professional body's supplier-audit course only if the firm posts a defined audit role, pays the fee and gives paid study hours; otherwise I would read its free guidance while keeping paid returns. Before or after 2031, I would take that posted audit job only with written wage, hours and start date covering our mortgage and confirmed pickup. If returns end before an offer, I would use the reserve for bills during the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the tax wage, but five years is enough to test a funded route. I will not buy a certificate to decorate the wall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the firm refuses paid study time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would keep the paid files available and use the free guidance. I would apply to other posted audit jobs only when their written terms cover our bills and pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could the audit role vanish too?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes, its screen checks face AGI as well. I would treat a real paid opening as a bridge and keep learning while it pays.

say: I would seek a **posted paid audit route**.
I would reject a **course without a job** behind it.
think: The **routine return fee** could fall by 2031.
My freight-document experience could support a **paid audit bridge** if a vacancy exists.
do: Read **free supplier guidance** while paid; enrol only for a posted role with funded fee and paid study hours.
Keep **paid returns** while offered; after loss, use the reserve for bills during search.
Take a **posted audit job** before or after 2031 only with written mortgage-covering wage, hours, start and pickup.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing the tax wage.
S3.quote: I will not buy a certificate to decorate the wall.
fieldNote: The course is actual enrolment only under **posted-role gates**, funded fees and paid time; free guidance preserves current income if refused.
He acknowledges that supplier audit remains **screen work** exposed to AGI, so a written offer is a bridge.

steps.text: Read free guidance; enrol only for posted role with funded fee and paid study hours
Keep paid returns while offered; after loss use reserve for bills
Take posted audit job with written mortgage-covering wage hours start and confirmed pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years gives me time to build a paying second line before AGI reaches accounts in 2036. Robots in 2039 come later for warehouse work, but they do not stretch the life of tax checking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the partners I intend to keep my existing clients properly served while I test a separate evening class. I would tell people a side project is income only when someone has booked and paid for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the firm's preparation fees may shrink by 2036, but fourteen months saved and many nearby firms let me test an alternative without leaving a good wage. I would not spend the reserve on an empty classroom.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would offer a monthly paid bookkeeping class for local repair shops only after my firm gives written permission, at least six shops book and pay, and Rina and I confirm the children's evening care. I would keep my paid accounting files while offered; in the first year after 2036, if the role ends, I would use the reserve for bills and continue the class only while paying bookings exist. I would take a posted senior accounting job only with written wage, hours and start date covering our mortgage and family schedule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about a distant loss of my main post, but a decade lets me learn whether a class actually pays. A room full of polite questions is not a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why six shops?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Fewer than six paid places would not cover the room and my time. I would cancel rather than use our reserve to make the class look busy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the firm refuses permission?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would keep the paid accounts work and drop the class. I do not want a side income that costs me the job I have.

say: I would keep **current clients** served while testing a paid class.
I would count **paid bookings**, not expressions of interest.
think: A class is income only if **six shops pay** and my employer permits it.
do: Run a **monthly bookkeeping class** only with written firm permission, six paid bookings and confirmed evening care; otherwise drop it.
Keep **paid accounts files** while offered; after loss use reserve for bills and continue only paying classes.
Take a **posted senior role** only with written mortgage-covering wage, hours, start and family-schedule fit.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about the later desk change.
S4.quote: A room full of polite questions is not a wage.
fieldNote: His side line has three gates: **written firm permission**, six paying shops and confirmed care.
After 2036 loss he uses the **existing reserve** for bills and keeps classes only while bookings truly pay.

steps.text: Run monthly class only with written firm permission six paid shops and confirmed evening care
Keep paid accounts while offered; after loss use reserve and run only paying classes
Take posted senior job with written mortgage-covering wage hours start and family fit

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it would cut my high wage before I could test a second paid line. Clear notice, written severance and actual posted work at a wage our family can live on would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether a business owner will pay for a class after saying it sounds useful. I have seen enough unpaid enthusiasm in the accounts to ask for a booking first.

headlineQuote: I have seen enough unpaid enthusiasm in the accounts to ask for a booking first.
portrait: Colin is a **43-year-old senior accountant** with a master's and chartered qualification who leads wholesaler accounts.
His **high wage**, fourteen-month reserve, mortgage and many nearby firms give his family choices.
He uses AI **daily** but requires paid tests and signed approval before a live change.
He tests a **paid bookkeeping class** under employer permission, bookings and evening-care conditions.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** world could remove his high wage before a second line pays.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **notice and severance**, plus a posted paid role that covers family bills.
